description: Fig. 2 is a full 12 x 12 correlation scatter-matrix (pair-plot) drawn in blue, with no panel letters — all cells are arranged in one grid. The twelve variables, in row and column order, are C (wt.%), Si (wt.%), Mn (wt.%), Cr (wt.%), S (wt.%), Ni (wt.%), P (wt.%), Fe (wt.%), Mo (wt.%), V (wt.%), W (wt.%) and Microhardness (HV); each label is printed on both the bottom x-axis and the left y-axis. The twelve diagonal cells hold filled light-blue probability-density histograms; the 132 off-diagonal cells are unfitted scatter plots of one variable against another using identical small blue circular markers. Every cell carries its own tick labels, e.g. C 1.5-2.0, Cr 5-10, Fe 80-90, P 0.05-0.15, W 0.5-1.5, Microhardness 400-600 HV. No correlation coefficient, p-value, regression line or data count is printed anywhere. Scatter cells involving Cr trend upward against Microhardness, Ni and Mo trend upward more weakly, while Fe (wt.%) forms a downward band against C, Cr, Ni and Mo — partly a compositional closure effect. The matrix is the correlation screen used before machine-learning prediction of microhardness.

observations.observation: The figure is a complete 12 x 12 scatter matrix in which both triangles are populated (no mirrored-cell suppression), so each variable pair appears twice with exchanged axes.

The variable labels printed on both the bottom axis and the left axis are, in order: C (wt.%), Si (wt.%), Mn (wt.%), Cr (wt.%), S (wt.%), Ni (wt.%), P (wt.%), Fe (wt.%), Mo (wt.%), V (wt.%), W (wt.%) and Microhardness (HV).
The 12 diagonal cells contain filled light-blue probability-density histograms rather than scatter points.

Printed tick values visible per axis include C 1.5 and 2.0; Si 0.5 and 1.0; Mn 1 and 2; Cr 5 and 10; S 0.5 and 1.0; Ni 1 and 2; P 0.05, 0.10 and 0.15; Fe 80, 85 and 90; Mo 0.5, 1.0 and 1.5; V 1 and 2; W 0.5, 1.0 and 1.5; Microhardness (HV) 400, 500 and 600.
Scatter cells of Cr (wt.%) against Microhardness (HV) show an upward trend, whereas Fe (wt.%) against C, Cr, Ni and Mo forms a distinctly downward-sloping band.
No correlation coefficient, p-value, regression line, confidence ellipse or dataset size is printed in any cell of the matrix.
Every off-diagonal cell uses the same marker style: small filled blue circles.
The caption consists only of the sentence "Fig. 2. Correlation scatter matrix graph." and names no variables, no sample and no numeric value.

The citing text states that the diagonal probability density histograms indicate Cr exhibits a positive correlation with microhardness, followed by Ni and Mo, whereas Mn, V and W showed weaker correlations.
The citing text states that Cr, Ni and Mo can form solid-solution alloys and carbides as strengthening phases, and that Ni can reduce the grain size of the alloys.
The citing text frames the figure as revealing the correlation between chemical composition and microhardness of the alloy.

subfigures.description: One filled light-blue probability-density histogram per variable (C, Si, Mn, Cr, S, Ni, P, Fe, Mo, V, W in wt.% and Microhardness (HV)), each with its own labelled tick marks on the outer axes. These histograms are the density plots the citing text uses to rank element-microhardness correlations.

Scatter plots of every variable pair, each cell with its own axis ticks; e.g. the Cr column against C, Si, Mn shows broad clouds, whereas Fe rows against C, Cr, Ni, Mo show clear downward-sloping bands. No fitted lines or correlation values are drawn.
Mirror images (axes exchanged) of the same variable pairs; they reproduce the same trends, e.g. Microhardness vs Cr rising and Microhardness vs Fe falling.

The Microhardness (HV) row and column, spanning roughly 400-600 HV on the y-axis of the last row, show the composition-microhardness relationships: upward trends with Cr, Ni and Mo and a downward trend with Fe.

unreadable_items: Bottom-axis tick labels of the Cr (wt.%) column appear inconsistent with the 5-10 range printed on that variable's y-axis; the small print is partially readable at the supplied resolution
Exact tick values for the Mn, Ni, Mo and V column axes are only partially legible
Number of data points per cell and any statistical significance values are not printed, so they cannot be extracted
